subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Measuring development and the development gap

questions.q: What does the economic indicator GNI stand for?
options: Gross National Income
General National Industry
Gross Natural Index
Global National Investment
questions.explain: GNI (Gross National Income) is the total value of goods and services produced by a country plus money earned from abroad, often given per head.

questions.q: Which three elements are combined to calculate the Human Development Index (HDI)?
options: Life expectancy, education and income
Birth rate, death rate and migration
Literacy, employment and housing
Health spending, GDP and trade
questions.explain: HDI combines life expectancy, education (years of schooling) and income (GNI per head) into a single figure between 0 and 1.

questions.q: Why is GNI per head on its own a limited measure of a country's development?
options: It is an average that can hide inequalities within a country
It cannot be calculated for HICs
It only measures a country's population size
It ignores a country's total wealth completely
questions.explain: As an average, GNI per head masks large gaps between rich and poor and says nothing about how wealth is shared.

questions.q: What does the infant mortality rate measure?
options: The number of deaths of children under one year per 1000 live births
The average number of children per woman
The percentage of children attending school
The number of adults who die each year per 1000 people
questions.explain: Infant mortality is the number of babies who die before their first birthday per 1000 live births, and is high in less developed countries.

questions.q: A country has a high birth rate but a rapidly falling death rate, causing very rapid population growth. Which stage of the Demographic Transition Model does this match?
options: Stage 2
Stage 1
Stage 4
Stage 5
questions.explain: In Stage 2 death rates fall sharply (better healthcare and food) while birth rates stay high, so the population grows rapidly.

questions.q: What is the main aim of Fair Trade?
options: To guarantee producers in LICs a fair, stable price for their goods
To remove all taxes on luxury imports
To provide emergency food after a disaster
To cancel the debts of the poorest countries
questions.explain: Fair Trade ensures farmers and workers in poorer countries receive a fair, guaranteed price so they get a better standard of living.

questions.q: How can the growth of tourism help reduce the development gap in an LIC or NEE?
options: It brings in foreign income and creates jobs and infrastructure
It reduces the country's total population
It removes the need for any foreign aid
It automatically ends all corruption
questions.explain: Tourism earns valuable foreign currency, provides employment and encourages investment in roads, airports and services.

questions.q: Which best describes intermediate (appropriate) technology?
options: Small-scale, affordable technology suited to local skills and conditions
The most advanced high-tech equipment available
Technology that only large TNCs can operate
Machinery imported entirely from HICs
questions.explain: Intermediate technology is simple, low-cost and matched to local needs and skills, such as hand pumps or efficient stoves.

questions.q: What are microfinance loans designed to do?
options: Provide small loans to individuals to help them start small businesses
Give large loans only to national governments
Cancel a country's international debt
Fund large-scale dam and road projects
questions.explain: Microfinance gives very small loans to ordinary people, often women, so they can set up small enterprises and improve their income.

questions.q: An LIC's foreign debts are cancelled so that the money it once spent on repayments can be used for schools and hospitals. Which strategy is this?
options: Debt relief
Fair Trade
Microfinance
Intermediate technology
questions.explain: Debt relief cancels or reduces a country's debts, freeing up money to invest in development such as health and education.

questions.q: In which region of Africa is Nigeria, a commonly studied NEE, located?
options: West Africa
North Africa
Southern Africa
East Africa
questions.explain: Nigeria lies in West Africa and has the largest population and one of the largest economies on the continent.

questions.q: Which transnational corporation (TNC) is closely associated with oil production in Nigeria?
options: Shell
Nestle
Toyota
Samsung
questions.explain: Shell is a major oil TNC operating in Nigeria's Niger Delta, bringing investment but also causing pollution.

questions.q: What is one advantage TNCs can bring to a country such as Nigeria?
options: They provide jobs and bring in investment and technology
They guarantee that all profits stay in the country
They remove the need for any government
They automatically prevent all pollution
questions.explain: TNCs create employment, invest money and introduce new skills and technology, boosting the wider economy.

questions.q: What is a disadvantage of TNCs operating in an NEE like Nigeria?
options: Much of the profit is sent back to the company's home country
They always pay the highest wages in the world
They provide free education to everyone
They never damage the local environment
questions.explain: A key drawback is that profits often flow overseas to the TNC's headquarters rather than benefiting the host nation.

questions.q: In the Niger Delta, pipelines leak and crops and fishing grounds are damaged. This is an example of which impact of economic development?
options: A negative environmental impact from oil production
A positive social impact of tourism
An improvement in the country's HDI
A benefit of intermediate technology
questions.explain: Oil spills pollute water and soil in the Niger Delta, harming ecosystems and the livelihoods that depend on farming and fishing.

questions.q: What does deindustrialisation mean?
options: The decline of manufacturing industry in a country
The rapid growth of heavy industry
An increase in a country's farming output
The building of new coal mines
questions.explain: Deindustrialisation is the decline of a country's manufacturing sector, which strongly affected UK industrial regions.

questions.q: Which type of work is typical of the quaternary sector that has grown in the UK's post-industrial economy?
options: Research, development and knowledge-based services
Coal and iron ore mining
Assembling cars in factories
Growing crops on farms
questions.explain: The quaternary sector involves research, development and high-tech knowledge work, often found on science and business parks.

questions.q: Which of the following is a cause of economic change in the UK?
options: Globalisation and government policy
A fall in the total world population
The discovery of gold in every city
The end of all international trade
questions.explain: Economic change in the UK has been driven by deindustrialisation, globalisation and government policies.

questions.q: What is meant by a 'post-industrial economy'?
options: An economy dominated by service and quaternary industries rather than manufacturing
An economy based only on farming
An economy with no service jobs at all
An economy that relies solely on coal and steel
questions.explain: A post-industrial economy is one where service, finance and high-tech quaternary industries have replaced traditional manufacturing.

questions.q: The government invests in improved rail links and enterprise zones across northern England to attract businesses. What is this mainly trying to achieve?
options: Reduce the north-south divide
Increase deindustrialisation
Lower the UK's life expectancy
Reduce the quaternary sector
questions.explain: Investing in transport and enterprise zones in the north aims to close the economic gap between the wealthier south and the north.

specSource: AQA GCSE Geography (8035) specification; The Changing Economic World
